Op. 2 = XII Sonate a doi, violin, viola da gamba and continuo, Nuremberg 1693; No. 2 in D minor, 11.0 min on cpo (Echo du Danube, 2020).
Key rightly left out of title: Tudor disc says C minor, Padrta/Wikipedia E-flat, IMSLP gives none. Published 1805 (IMSLP); Tudor 22.7 min.

Silvertrust: composed 1795, new edition based on the 1796 Gombart edition (Augsburg). IMSLP's 'c. 1810' is not supported (Op. 4 was out in 1794, Op. 7 c. 1797). Title, movements, 15.9 min (Martinu Quartet, Supraphon) fine.
Authentic Quartet, Hungaroton 2009: key and movement order match the notes, 22.6 min. Op. 7 published by Andre c. 1797 (Wikipedia list).
Authentic Quartet, Hungaroton 2009: key and movement order match the notes, 24.2 min. Op. 7 published by Andre c. 1797 (Wikipedia list).
Authentic Quartet, Hungaroton 2009: key and movement order match the notes, 22.9 min. Op. 7 published by Andre c. 1797 (Wikipedia list).
Six movements, Eybler dedication, 1818 Steiner print (IMSLP); Kontraste Koln 39 min, Czech String Trio 43 min.

E-flat = Op. 21 No. 1 on CPO, Tudor and IMSLP (Supraphon/Padrta swap the numbers; aka covers it); 4 movements with Romanza, 17-24 min on three discs. Year 1802 not independently sourced (Wikipedia mentions an Andre edition of 1819).
B-flat = Op. 21 No. 2 on CPO, Tudor and IMSLP (Supraphon/Padrta swap the numbers); 4 movements, 16-24 min on three discs. Year 1802 not independently sourced.
Three discs (CPO, Tudor, Musica viva), 4 movements Allegro moderato/Adagio/Minuetto/Rondo; Silvertrust: published 1816, D major.
CPO (Kloecker) plays it in 3 movements, 18.5 min. 'Op. posth.' is the CPO label; Padrta lists it only as P IX:B1 (in aka).
13 pieces for 2 clarinets and viola, Op. 47 (P XII:1): Tudor 27 min, Da Vinci 35 min.
IMSLP 1799, 4 movements; Claves (Graf, Carmina Trio) 21.9 min.

Key: the Meier/Stamitz disc plays Op. 63 in D major, but Padrta (P VII:5) and Wikipedia's opus list give C major. No IMSLP page; exists and recorded (24.9 min). Year 1808 unsourced.

Three movements with central Menuetto (Tudor 14.2 min, Ars 15.7 min); rediscovered, first published 1959 (MusicWeb).

Naxos 2006 (Nancy Ambrose King) calls it Oboe Quartet No. 3 in F major, 4 movements as in notes, 22.2 min. Padrta lists only two oboe quartets (P IX:21-22), so no P number; the numbering is the label's.
Naxos 2006, 4 movements, 27.1 min; Regis review confirms oboe, violin, two violas, cello; P VII:12 in Padrta.
Naxos 2006, 23.9 min, finale Andante poco Allegretto; P VII:13 in Padrta.
Bassoon, 2 violas, cello; CPO 20.3 min, Ars 22.4 min; P IX:8; recorded on four labels.
Bassoon, 2 violas, cello; CPO 20.8 min, Ars 23.5 min; Adagio second, Rondo finale; P IX:9.
Op. 16 on the cpo disc and in MusicWeb (Wikipedia says Op. 17, already in aka); 38.7 min. MusicWeb dates it 1878 and says Krug was 29 (born Oct 1849), Wikipedia 1879: use the span.

Key unsettled: Naxos, Brilliant and Wikipedia say E major; Sony (Rampal/Juilliard) and IMSLP's comment say E minor with an E major introduction (Allegro agitato). All else holds (4 movements, 28 min, Simrock 1823, three recordings). Drop the key if it cannot be settled from the score.

1698 Kassel print: Nos. 1-6 are for two violas da gamba, Nos. 7-14 solo; No. 3 in G minor is six variations on a ground, 9.6 min on the Dunford album (four players credited). Preface lets Nos. 1-3 go without continuo.

note: Krommer dominates the chunk. Open points: Krommer Op. 63 key (D major on the recording, C major in Padrta/Wikipedia), Kuhlau Op. 51 No. 2 key (E major vs E minor), Krieger 'Op. 1' (presumed from Op. 2 = 1693), Oboe Quartet No. 3 has no Padrta number, Op. 21 clarinet quartets numbered differently on Supraphon.
